gen-gf-gabarito-gf-philosopher: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open. Its round letters bend like wire and carry the personality, while the plain sans Philosopher handles the reading with gentle shifts in thickness.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-pt-sans: Expressive from the first letter, Gabarito leaves its terminals cut open. It makes the louder statement, while PT Sans, a sans-serif with open-arc c forms, does the approachable everyday work of the text.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Wide-set letters with generous clearance and round forms like open parentheses give Goldman its bold, commanding look. Kdam Thmor Pro, a modern sans, then takes over with line-filling bowls.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-tiny5: Goldman sets wide, commanding letters whose lowercase stands tall against its capitals, with round forms like open parentheses. Tiny5, an approachable sans, settles in beneath it with short-looking ascenders.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-voces: Commanding in every wide-set letter, Goldman gives its round forms the look of open parentheses. Voces, a sans with gentle stroke modulation, steadies all the text beneath it.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-winky-rough: Bold from edge to edge, Goldman sets wide, generous letters and round forms that read like open parentheses. Winky Rough, plain sans with lowercase nearly matching the capitals, trails quietly.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-winky-sans: Goldman's wide-set letters and round, parenthesis-like forms give every heading a bold, commanding stance. Winky Sans, a modern sans-serif with capitals barely taller than its lowercase, then reads smoothly over paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-inder: Round, open and sturdy: Grandstander keeps one line width throughout. What holds the pair together is that Inder, a sans-serif with little height difference between cases, lets the heading's tall x-height stand out.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-mukta: Round, bold, no contrast: Grandstander draws every stroke alike. Mukta, plain sans with tall-bodied small letters, settles into a clean, neutral run of text and never competes with the heading above it.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-clash-grotesk: Clash Grotesk, the sans-serif here, has no stroke modulation at all. Happy Monkey does the attention-grabbing work with ruler-straight lines and wide gaps in the e, while the body font keeps things approachable.
